      RESEARCH
      Learning physical systems for control and optimization.
      My research asks how a learned model should represent dynamics and uncertainty when its outputs determine a schedule, control action, or physical design. I study this question through probabilistic prediction, operator learning, closed-loop analysis, and constrained physical optimization.
    
    
      
        Decision-focused forecasting under uncertainty
        Probabilistic forecasts are trained and evaluated through the schedules, costs, and constraints they induce. Work on water-demand timing and uncertain pressure regression further identifies when prediction errors occur and which unobserved effects they represent.
      
      
        Neural operators for distributed dynamics
        I study maps from initial conditions, geometry, boundary conditions, and forcing fields to spatiotemporal solutions. Field error, rollout error, and sensitivity error measure how accurately the learned operator represents the dynamics used in control and optimization.
      
      
        Learning-based control
        I examine how approximation error accumulates over a control horizon and changes the selected action, closed-loop cost, and constraint violation. These quantities provide control-specific criteria for training and evaluating learned physical dynamics.
      
      
        Constrained optimization of physical systems
        I study differentiable solution operators inside constrained design and operating problems, including experiment selection, process control, and materials design. Gradient accuracy and feasibility determine whether the learned model preserves the optimized decision.
      
    
    Methods and research questions

title: Urban water forecasting and pressure modeling
text:
Daily urban water-demand forecasts can attain low average error while responding late when demand changes direction. This lag reduces their value for planning the next operating period.
The knowledge-based bi-correction model addresses the problem in two stages. Lag-penalty attention extracts prior sequence and feature information associated with timely demand changes. A stacked LSTM produces the primary forecast. A masked weighted Markov chain then corrects selected residuals using posterior error information.

title: Urban water forecasting and pressure modeling
text:
Trend-sensitive evaluation
The study introduces mean prediction trend effectiveness to test whether a model follows changes in demand more closely than a naive forecast. Reporting this metric alongside absolute-error measures separates response timing from average numerical accuracy.

title: Urban water forecasting and pressure modeling
text:
Pressure under unobserved variation
CritiCoder considers macroscopic pressure when measured inputs do not explain every disturbance in a water distribution system. Its Coder models the response associated with observed variables, while the Critic changes the loss so that the remaining pressure variation can be represented as an uncertain disturbance.
The comparison tests whether CritiCoder’s error increases less than conventional regression error at nodes more strongly affected by unobserved disturbances.

title: Research
text:
My research asks how learned models of physical systems can support control and optimization under dynamics, uncertainty, and constraints. Across coupled water–energy systems and materials processes, I evaluate predictive models through the schedules, actions, and physical designs they inform.
This topic includes four closely related directions. Decision-focused forecasting identifies which predictive errors change operating decisions. Neural operators learn maps between physical conditions and distributed state trajectories. Learning-based control examines how model error affects actions over a control horizon. Constrained physical optimization studies whether learned solution maps preserve useful gradients and feasible decisions. These directions share one criterion. The learned model should represent the physical quantities that determine the downstream decision.

title: Research
text:
Decision-focused forecasting under uncertainty
Forecast errors matter differently when predictions determine an operating schedule. In coupled water–energy systems, Stochastic Predict-Then-Optimize trains probabilistic electricity-cost forecasts through the stochastic water-supply schedules they induce. A differentiable upper bound on optimality gap passes changes in scheduling cost back to the predictor.
Work on lag-free demand forecasting and uncertain pressure regression examines two additional sources of prediction error. Lag-penalty attention targets delayed reactions near demand turning points, while uncertain regression separates modeled responses to observed inputs from residual pressure variation associated with unobserved disturbances. These studies relate forecast accuracy to operating cost, decision sensitivity, and constraint satisfaction.

title: Research
text:
Neural operators for distributed dynamics
Many control and design problems depend on physical fields that evolve across space and time. I study neural operators that map initial conditions, geometry, boundary conditions, and forcing fields to spatiotemporal solution fields. Their evaluation includes field error, rollout error, and the sensitivities used by control and optimization.

title: Research
text:
Learning-based control
A learned solution operator can supply state rollouts without solving the governing equations from scratch at every control step. I study how approximation error accumulates over a control horizon and changes the selected action, closed-loop cost, and constraint violation. These quantities provide control-specific criteria for training and evaluating learned physical dynamics.

title: Research
text:
Constrained optimization and materials processes
Constrained optimization depends on accurate state trajectories, local sensitivities, and feasible decisions. I study differentiable solution operators inside design and operating problems, with attention to whether surrogate gradients preserve the selected decision. Objective value, feasibility, and decision sensitivity provide the main evaluation quantities.
Materials processes provide a field-evolving setting for this work. Learned solution maps can support experiment selection, process control, and constrained design when the physical state evolves across space and time.

title: Research
text:
Related collaborative work
Collaborative work on generated actions examines how learned trajectories satisfy geometric and decision constraints. DRIFT stores local LiDAR geometry as graph memory during recurrent diffusion and evaluates the generated motion through endpoint error, clearance, smoothness, and runtime.

title: Water-energy resource scheduling
text:
Urban water supply consumes electricity throughout treatment, transport, and distribution. The resulting schedule depends on the expected electricity cost, while errors in that forecast can change operating cost and the selected schedule.
The study models the full water-supply process as a stochastic scheduling problem with uncertain electricity prices. Forecast quality is evaluated both by pointwise prediction error and by the objective value of the induced schedule.

title: Water-energy resource scheduling
text:
Stochastic Predict-Then-Optimize
Stochastic Predict-Then-Optimize combines a probabilistic forecasting model with the downstream stochastic program. Its forecast distribution supplies uncertain cost parameters to the scheduler, and the resulting schedule defines the decision loss used to update the predictor.
Direct differentiation through this optimization problem is difficult. SPTO+ replaces the exact optimality gap with a differentiable convex upper bound derived from Lagrangian duality. The bound supplies a surrogate gradient while retaining the scheduling problem in the training objective.

title: Water-energy resource scheduling
text:
Evaluation
Experiments on real-world water-supply systems compare forecast quality, operating cost, and decision regret. SPTO reports lower operating cost and regret than the tested two-stage forecasting and optimization baselines.
